title: Hawaii's 2nd Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Hawaii's 2nd Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Democrat Jill Tokuda, first elected in 2022, is seeking a third term representing a district that covers rural and suburban Oahu as well as all of Hawaii's neighbor islands (Hawaii, Maui, Kauai, and Molokai). Tokuda faces a challenge from Republican state Senator Brenton Awa, the Minority Leader of the Hawaii Senate, in a district rated Safe/Solid Democratic by all major forecasters (Cook PVI: D+12). Major issues include recovery from the 2023 Maui wildfires, housing affordability, and economic diversification.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election in Hawaii's 2nd Congressional District as of mid-2026. The race is rated 'Solid D' / 'Safe D' by Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball.

candidates.name: Jill Tokuda
candidates.summary: Jill Tokuda is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Hawaii's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024 with 66.5% of the vote. She previously served in the Hawaii State Senate from 2006 to 2018, where she chaired the Ways and Means Committee, and was the executive director of the Nisei Veterans Memorial Center on Maui. Tokuda serves on the House Agriculture and Armed Services Committees and has focused on recovery from the 2023 Maui wildfires, supporting working families, and protecting the environment.

candidates.name: Brenton Awa
candidates.summary: Brenton Awa is a Hawaii State Senator representing District 23 (Kaneohe to Mokuleia) and serves as the Senate Minority Leader, a position he has held since 2024. A former television news anchor and reporter for KITV, Awa was first elected to the state Senate in 2022 after an upset victory over an eight-year incumbent. He has gained attention for casting over 1,000 'no' votes in his first two legislative sessions and for his advocacy of policies to restrict foreign ownership of land in Hawaii. Awa is challenging incumbent Democrat Jill Tokuda for the 2nd Congressional District seat.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling is available for this race, which tempers confidence in the exact margin. However, the district's structural fundamentals are overwhelming: Cook PVI of D+12, all major nonpartisan forecasters rate it Safe/Solid Democratic, and incumbent Democrat Jill Tokuda won re-election in 2024 with 66.5% of the vote. Republican challenger Brenton Awa is a credible candidate (state Senate Minority Leader) with a distinct profile, but the district's strong Democratic lean, Tokuda's incumbency advantage, and the lack of any recent competitive performance for Republicans in this seat make a Democratic hold virtually certain. The margin estimate of ~24 points reflects a slight moderation from 2024's 33-point margin due to Awa's potential appeal on local issues (foreign land ownership, Maui recovery) but still reflects a very safe Democratic seat.
